title: The Harbor Test: Hopeful science-fiction adventure
retrieval_query: dramatic irony competing obligations planted clues reversal consequences
reference_policy: Optional craft guidance only; never import another work’s facts, genre, characters or style.
reader_experience: Distinct voices, escalating choices and a surprising but retrospectively supported turn.
pov: Present-tense filmable or performable action. Limit private knowledge to actual witnesses; follow the selected script medium.
tone_mood: Hopeful science-fiction adventure with specific human stakes and varied emotional pacing.
sensory_detail: Select details appropriate to the medium; audio establishes action through sound, comics through drawable panels.
ending_tendency: Resolve this episode’s main choice with an earned reversal and a lasting consequence; leave one meaningful unresolved thread.
premise: A young courier must carry a fragile seed bank across a floating city while two factions dispute who gets the first harvest. Develop 2 connected scenes. Invent the decisive discovery and climax yourself; no exact solution, culprit or twist is prescribed. Plant observable evidence before any revelation and make the climax change a relationship and consume a real advantage.

length_policy.policy: 2 scenes, target 300 words each; strict allowed range 240–390. Script cues count toward words; no padding.

adaptation.divergence: Invent solutions and climax; do not import film or epic canon.

style.narrator: Follow the selected medium; do not add internal narration to scripts.
style.register: Hopeful science-fiction adventure; original language, economical exposition, no generic moral.
wording: No borrowed quotations, catchphrases or stock epic imagery.
Do not repeat earlier negotiations, discoveries or explanations.
style.interiority: Show conflicting obligations through choices; prose may access only its focal viewpoint.
style.dialogue: Distinct motives and speech patterns; use subtext and changing leverage.

world_rules: Only this brief and accepted on-page events are canon.
Private beliefs and clues cannot leak without an enacted disclosure.
Mara and Ivo remain siblings, with stable names and identities.
Every token or radio transmission is counted at its actual expenditure.
Physical travel, entrances and exits need an explicit cause and interval.
No retroactive backup power, extra token, secret tunnel or unearned rescue.
Plans, suspicions and hypotheses are not completed history.
Any extraordinary mechanism must be established with limits before solving a conflict.
Different medium presentation never changes underlying facts.
Costs, injuries, custody and consequences persist.
A twist needs an observable setup before payoff; no new retrospective facts to explain it.
Only the current scene participants may act unless a new entrance is established.

Mara holds exactly two single-use ferry passage tokens. Each token permits one ferry crossing; spent tokens cannot return.
Ivo holds one portable radio with power for two outbound transmissions; receiving uses no counted transmission.
Mara and Ivo are siblings; neither has told the other their private household promise.
Sera alone knows that one archive ledger has an erased date; she has not identified who erased it or why.
Travel among the four locations requires visible departure and arrival or an explicit interval of at least ten minutes.
The quay connects the districts; the tower relays calls; the archive holds records; the council chamber hosts public decisions.

world_design.setting: A harbor city with four districts linked by a ferry quay, signal tower, archive and council chamber.
world_design.technology: Genre-appropriate tools constrained by the authored resource limits.
world_design.institutions: Harbor authority, district council, archive and household obligations.
world_design.physical_systems: A limited ferry service and radio; travel takes time.
world_design.deadlines: The public decision occurs by the next dawn; establish changes to the deadline explicitly.

plot_design.central_question: Who bears the cost when a city keeps one promise by breaking another?
causal_dependencies: Later scenes inherit actual knowledge, resources and changed relationships.
An invented clue must be enacted before the climax uses it.

subplots.question: Can the siblings disagree without making each other expendable?
subplots.intersection: The public choice forces a private concession.
subplots.removal_cost: The decision loses its human stakes.

alternatives_and_costs: Spend a scarce advantage to disclose evidence, or protect a dependent while conceding leverage.

quality_contract: Respect the selected medium, its headings, tense, cues and representable action.
Distinct voices and conflicting aims must cause choices, not inventory exposition.
Connect all scenes through full authoritative memory, with no repetition or reset.
Check exact custody, counted resources, character knowledge, chronology and geography.
Final climax must reinterpret an earlier enacted clue or choice; surprise cannot depend on a retroactively invented fact.
The original outcome is not prescribed; assess source-supported originality and consequences rather than conformity to a hidden plot.

must_avoid: Imported Marvel, Homeric or other external canon.
Recapping an earlier negotiation instead of progressing.
Instant offstage construction, unexplained reserves, or leaks of private information.
Adding prose narration to a script or headings to prose.

execution_intent.authorized: User requested sequential live stress tests across formats, genres, lengths and larger worlds.
execution_intent.workflow: Full separate-runner pipeline; strict literary and factual gates; Gemini waits and no automatic local downgrade.
